import pandas as pd

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

# Display the first few rows and the data types
df.head(), df.dtypes

# Check for missing values in the dataset
missing_values = df.isnull().sum()
missing_values[missing_values > 0]

# Drop rows with missing values
df_cleaned = df.dropna()

# Check the shape of the cleaned dataset
df_cleaned.shape

from lifelines import KaplanMeierFitter

# Initialize the Kaplan-Meier fitter
kmf = KaplanMeierFitter()

# Fit the model using follow_up_time and event_observed
kmf.fit(durations=df_cleaned['follow_up_time'], event_observed=df_cleaned['event_observed'])

# Plot the Kaplan-Meier survival curve
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
kmf.plot_survival_function()
plt.title('Kaplan-Meier Survival Curve')
plt.xlabel('Follow Up Time')
plt.ylabel('Survival Probability')
plt.grid()
plt.show()

# Calculate the median survival time
median_survival_time = kmf.median_survival_time_
median_survival_time

from lifelines import CoxPHFitter

# Prepare the data for the Cox model
cox_data = df_cleaned[['gender', 'body_mass_index', 'blood_pressure', 'cholesterol_level', 'follow_up_time', 'event_observed']]

# Initialize and fit the Cox Proportional Hazards model
cph = CoxPHFitter()
cph.fit(cox_data, duration_col='follow_up_time', event_col='event_observed')

# Get the summary of the Cox model
cox_summary = cph.summary

# Extract the p-value for the model and the hazard ratio for 'body_mass_index'
p_value = cox_summary.loc['body_mass_index', 'p']  # p-value
hazard_ratio_bmi = cox_summary.loc['body_mass_index', 'exp(coef)']  # Hazard ratio

p_value, hazard_ratio_bmi
